deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page, dated 29.11.83). X is a compact oriented surface with boundary. Each boundary component T_i, i in I = pi_0(dX), carries a 'toric structure': it is made a torsor under U = {|z|=1}, i.e. given a parametrization up to rotation.

- SRT(X) is the group of automorphisms of X preserving the orientation and the toric structures, modulo the identity component of the subgroup inducing the identity on dX.
- It contains a canonical normal subgroup R^I of boundary rotations, lifted to the universal cover. Inside R^I sits Z^I, the full-turn rotations, i.e. the boundary Dehn twists.
- SUT(X) = SRT(X)/Z^I, and there is an extension (*) 1 -> U^I -> SUT(X) -> T(X) -> 1.

This page.
1. Splitting. A choice of base points s = (s_i), one s_i in each T_i, gives a splitting phi_s : T(X) -> SUT(X) of (*): take the classes of automorphisms fixing the base points.
2. The subgroup. S_1T(X,s), the mapping class group of X with one marked point on each boundary circle, is identified with the inverse image of phi_s(T(X)) under SRT(X) -> SUT(X). This explains the formula of the previous page, S_1T(X,s) wedge^{Z^I} R^I = SRT(X). Equivalently, SRT is the pushout of the central Z^I-extension along Z^I -> R^I.
3. Change of base point. Replacing s by s' = u.s with u in U^I conjugates the splitting: phi_{s'} = int(u) o phi_s. Lifting u to some u~ in R^I gives S_1T(X,s') = int(u~) S_1T(X,s).
4. Modular versus non-modular data. On the surface X-bar, the choice of s is 'non-modular'. SRT(X) depends only on the 'modular' datum, namely the toric structures. The product of the T_i, as a U^I-torsor, is identified with the torsor of splittings of (*), with U^I acting by inner automorphisms. The ambiguity of the lifts to R^I is exactly Z^I.
5. Margin diagram. Two arrows into SRT(X): one from R^I and one from S_1T^!(X).

Purpose. This is groundwork for the 'Teichmüller tower' of Esquisse d'un programme (1984). It gives a base-point-free group SRT(X) of the surface with toric boundary, into which the various mapping class groups with marked boundary points embed canonically up to conjugation. The next page extends this to 'multiconfigurations', 1/n_i Z-subtorsors on the boundary.
errors: The transcribed 'SUR(X) -> SUT(X)' must mean SRT(X) -> SUT(X).
The subgroup is the INVERSE image of phi_s(T(X)) under the projection. 'Image directe' is crossed out in the manuscript, and 'image inverse' is what the mathematics requires.

The notation is inconsistent across pages: S_*T, S_1T and S_1T^! appear to denote related groups (with or without permutations of boundary components), as Grothendieck himself flags in the margin of the previous page.
No mathematical error. Conjugation by u~ is well defined on S_1T(X,s) because the ambiguity Z^I lies in S_1T(X,s).

ideas.what: Splitting of the rotation extension 1 -> U^I -> SUT(X) -> T(X) by a choice of boundary base points; boundary-pointed mapping class groups recovered as inverse images of the splitting.
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of a surface with marked boundary points as a central Z^I-extension; boundary-twist / framing extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Dehn twist central extension). Used in CFT contexts by Moore–Seiberg (1989), Segal, and Bakalov–Kirillov (extended surfaces, ~2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower with boundary/base-point data, but not this explicit group-theoretic formalism

ideas.what: The base-point-independent group SRT(X) = S_1T(X,s) wedge^{Z^I} R^I, the pushout of the Dehn-twist subgroup Z^I into R^I. It depends only on the toric (modular) data, with the pointed subgroups conjugate under R^I.
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of a surface with boundary parametrized up to rotation, with real boundary twists (an R-extension used for framing/conformal anomaly considerations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Segal's CFT formalism and in Bakalov–Kirillov / Funar-type extended mapping class groups; not standardly attributed

ideas.what: The torsor of base-point choices (product of the T_i) identified with the U^I-torsor of splittings of (*) under inner action; distinction between modular and non-modular data.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of splittings / conjugacy class of sections of an extension with abelian kernel

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1983 formalizes a base-point-free 'Teichmüller group of a surface with toric boundary' SRT(X), containing R^I, in which all pointed and (next page) 'multiconfigured' mapping class groups embed canonically up to conjugation. This is a careful precursor to later 'extended surface' groupoids in modular functor theory. It is not a new result, but the intrinsic R^I formulation is a historical detail of the Teichmüller tower programme not documented in Esquisse.
missed.quote: la définition de S_1T(X,s) dépend du choix s non-modulaire, par contre celle de S_1RT(X) ne dépend que d'un choix modulaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows that Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower was designed with boundary-rotation (R^I) extensions, anticipating the framing extensions of Bakalov–Kirillov / Moore–Seiberg Lego-Teichmüller constructions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine extension and splitting bookkeeping for mapping class groups of surfaces with parametrized boundary. Its intrinsic, modular-versus-non-modular framing is a nice historical detail but mathematically standard.
transcription_corrections: 'SUR(X) -> SUT(X)' should read SRT(X) -> SUT(X) (intended meaning).
'l'image [-inverse-] de' — the crossed-out word appears to be 'directe' (followed by 'de'); the intended sense is inverse image.

'De plus, TT_i [?] comme torseur sous U^I de relations (par fidélité modulaire)' probably reads 'De plus, ∏T_i, comme torseur sous U^I, s'identifie (par fidélité modulaire) à celui des scindages de l'ext. (*) (via action int. par U^I)'.
'[dédiés de SRT(X) aux structures simpl.]' is perhaps '[déduit de SRT(X) avec ses structures suppl.]'.
'souvenir [?] les relations [?] coincident avec Z^I' perhaps reads 'savoir: les relèvements ... coïncident avec Z^I' (the ambiguity of lifts to R^I is Z^I).
